 -2-  NC: 2023:KHC-D:10309  MFA No. 101247 of 2023  THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
JUDGMENT
The claimants in LAC No.118/2011 are before this Court challenging the judgment and award passed by the Court of Additional Senior Civil Judge, Jamkhandi.
The land bearing Sy.No.35/2 measuring 1 acre 3 guntas of Kurugod village, Taluk Jamkhandi has been acquired for Hipparagi project.
Section 4(1) notification was issued on 28.09.2006.
The Land Acquisition Officer passed an award granting compensation of Rs.64,904/- per acre treating acquired land as dry land.
2. Aggrieved by the aforementioned award of the Land Acquisition Officer, the claimantss sought reference before the Reference Court.

The Reference Court awarded compensation of Rs.3,05,500/-
per acre treating the acquired land as irrigated land.
Aggrieved by the aforementioned judgment and award, the appellants are before this Court seeking enhancement of compensation.

4. The learned counsel for the appellants would submit that the market value determined by this Court in MFA No.102782/2020, 102783/2020 and 102784/2020 disposed of on 30.03.2021 would also apply to the present case as in the aforementioned cases, this Court has fixed the market value in respect of the wet land acquired for Hipparagi project located in Athani taluk and Jamkhandi taluk.

5. He would also submit that the land which is the subject matter of this appeal is the wet land and it is the finding given by the Reference Court and this finding is not questioned by the beneficiary.
6. He submits that in the aforementioned cases, the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court awarded Rs.5,00,000/- per acre as the compensation for the wet land.

Thus, he would urge that the appellants are entitled NC: 2023:KHC-D:10309 to Rs.5,00,000/- per acre as the compensation for Smt. Shobha W/O. Bhimappa Vajrawad vs The Special Land Acquisition Officer on 8 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98855425/
2
the land acquired.

7. The learned counsel for the appellants would also submit that the beneficiary has taken a decision to award Rs.5,00,000/- per acre as the compensation for all the irrigated land which are acquired for Hipparagi project, acquired between 2004 and 2007.
Thus, he would submit that the appellants are also entitled to compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- per acre as the appellants' land was acquired in the year 2005.

8. The learned counsel appearing for respondent-beneficiary is not in a position to deny the above said submission as the Coordinate Bench of this Court has already passed an award in several cases granting Rs.5,00,000/- per acre as valuation of the irrigated land and the aforementioned judgments have not been questioned by the beneficiary and a statement is made at the Bar that the beneficiary has deposited NC: 2023:KHC-D:10309 Rs.5,00,000/- per acre as the compensation for wet land which have been acquired between 2004 to 2007.

9. The learned counsel for the appellants has also produced the Form No.C submitted by the beneficiary before the Reference Court, wherein the compensation amount is deposited at the rate of Rs.5,00,000/- per acre with all other consequential benefits.
10. The learned counsel appearing for the respondents are not in a position to dispute Form No.C said to have been filed before the Reference Court.
11. For the above mentioned reasons, this Court is of the view that the appellants are entitled to Rs.5,00,000/- per acre as the compensation for the land acquired with all statutory benefits.

12. However, it is made clear that since there was delay in filing the appeal and the delay was condoned subject to the condition that the appellants are not entitled to the interest for the delayed period in case compensation NC: 2023:KHC-D:10309 is enhanced, the appellants are not entitled to the interest for the delayed period of 2590 days.

Accordingly, the following:
ORDER i. Appeal is allowed in part.
 ii.
The judgment and award dated  30.08.2013 passed by the Additional  Senior Civil Judge, Jamkhandi, in  L.A.C.No.118/2011 are modified.
iii. The appellants are entitled for the compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- per acre in respect of the land acquired.
iv. The appellants are not entitled to the interest for the delayed period of 2590 days in respect of the enhanced compensation.
